supported_facts.statement: Development Notice: Senpai is a product in active development by InGen Dynamics. Features and capabilities described reflect our current design intent and development roadmap. Specifications are subject to change.

This page details the planned systems architecture, hardware specifications, sensor suite, compute platform, AI model implementation, security design, and V-Model development process for Senpai. All specifications represent current design intent and are subject to change during development and engineering validation.

Senpai's pedagogical framework draws on the most robustly evidenced methods in educational psychology: retrieval practice, spaced repetition, elaborative interrogation, and multimodal encoding. These are not buzzwords — they are the approaches with the strongest and most replicated evidence base for long-term learning.

Senpai's 720p projector (with an engineering upgrade path to 1080p) is designed to cast interactive content onto any nearby surface — a table, a floor, a wall — at up to 100 inches from 1.5 metres. Auto-keystone correction and autofocus are designed to make surface calibration automatic.

The projector system uses a depth camera to map the projection surface and track finger position at up to 60 frames per second — making the projected surface interactive. Children are designed to be able to tap, drag, and draw directly on the projected content.

Senpai's data is designed to surface differently for each stakeholder — the teacher needs teaching intelligence, the student needs a learning adventure, and the parent needs transparency in plain language.

The same underlying session data surfaces entirely differently depending on who is looking at it and why. The design system enforces strict context separation — teacher intelligence, student adventure, parent transparency, and admin governance are never mixed on a single screen.

Senpai's approach to language learning is being built around one principle: that conversation produces fluency faster than vocabulary memorisation. The system is designed to prioritise getting children speaking as early as possible, then building grammar and vocabulary knowledge to support and extend that conversation.

Pronunciation coaching is designed to use spectral audio analysis to compare a student's pronunciation against age-appropriate reference models for each language — giving feedback that is specific, actionable, and kind.

The EAL (English as Additional Language) module is designed as a separate configuration — delivering curriculum content in a student's home language while gradually increasing the proportion of English as their confidence grows.

SEND is not a feature we added to Senpai. It is a primary design constraint that has shaped every hardware and software decision from day one. This page describes our inclusion framework, our six adaptation modes, and the child safety architecture we are building.

Each adaptation mode represents a comprehensive set of interaction design decisions — not a checklist of visual adjustments. Every mode is designed to be activatable individually or in combination, recognising that many students have overlapping needs.

SEOM — the Safety and Ethics Operations Model — is a set of 12 rules being designed to govern every Senpai interaction with a child. Rather than relying on post-generation content filtering, these rules are intended to be embedded at the AI training objective level: the model is designed not to learn unsafe interaction patterns in the first place.

Rather than building for one regulatory framework and retrofitting for others, Senpai's design is intended to satisfy the intersection of the most demanding requirements across all target markets simultaneously. Note: compliance validation will be conducted through appropriate certification bodies during the development process — the frameworks below describe design intent.

Senpai's architecture implements a three-tier design: edge compute (on the robot) for real-time student interaction, a local classroom server for coordination and MIS integration, and cloud infrastructure for fleet management and model training. Core learning functions are designed to run on-device, with cloud connectivity optional rather than required.
Eye-Gaze Camera | IR 120 fps · 1280×720 · near-IR LEDs | Gaze input for PD students · attention tracking (ADHD) · reading pattern analysis (dyslexia) | PD Mode: full curriculum eye-gaze navigation
Noise Sensor | MEMS mic · 30–130 dB SPL | Classroom noise monitoring · audio quality gate · teacher alert on excessive noise | ASC: sensory protocol when >65 dB · ADHD: ventilation-linked attention
CO₂ Sensor | SCD41 · 400–5000 ppm · ±50 ppm | Classroom ventilation alert (>1000 ppm = attention decline signal) · teacher notification | ADHD: linked to attention capacity monitoring
GRPO | Goal-Reward Policy Optimisation | Edge (INT8 quantised) | <15 ms (TensorRT) | 30 M (edge) / 120 M (full)
SEOM | Safety & Ethics Oversight Model | Edge (critical path) | <5 ms | 5 M (8-bit quantised)
STUM | Spatio-Temporal Uncertainty Model | Edge (lightweight) | <10 ms | TBD during development

Security architecture is designed to meet or exceed COPPA, GDPR Article 32, FERPA, and UK DPA 2018 requirements. All student-facing data flows are designed with privacy-by-default: raw audio and video are not retained, no PII appears in logs, and biometric data is processed on-device only.
Student Privacy | No PII in logs · zero raw audio/video retention · anonymised analytics only · parent consent-gated parent app | COPPA §312.8 · GDPR Article 6(1)(a)
Biometric Design | Gaze and expression data processed on-device only · no biometric profiles designed to persist beyond session end | GDPR Article 9 · COPPA
Data Deletion | Parent-initiated deletion via app within 24 hours · automated 90-day retention policy for session logs | GDPR Article 17 · COPPA

Senpai development follows the V-Model systems engineering lifecycle — requirements flow down the left side (decomposition into 9 subsystems), implementation at the bottom, and verification/validation flows up the right side. Seven parallel development tracks run concurrently: HW, FW, AI/PIC 2.0, BE, APP, and INT.

Student (who needs joy and challenge), teacher (who needs insight and time-saving), parent (who needs transparency), and SENCO (who needs evidence). These six principles define how every interface decision is made.

Senpai's motion language is warm but purposeful. Achievement animations are designed to activate the reward system. LED ring states communicate emotion and activity to the entire classroom without words. All animations are capped at ≤3 Hz to prevent photosensitive responses — SEOM E01 enforces this at the animation system level.

Senpai's 13 planned screen layouts span the student robot display (10.1″ AMOLED), the teacher desktop dashboard, student learning adventure, parent mobile app, and admin interface. Each is designed for a distinct user, context, and purpose.

PIC 2.0 is the shared cognitive architecture across all InGen robots — designed to take a robot from raw sensor input to safe physical action in one unbroken sequence. All safety-critical decisions run on-device without network dependency.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0019 | paragraph | Six models. One pipeline. > From raw sensor to action — in one loop]
A core design principle: safety isn't a post-hoc filter — it's a mathematical constraint during model training itself. By the time a robot is deployed, the AI structurally cannot generate unsafe actions. They were never learned.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0025 | paragraph | The six models inside PIC 2.0]
Each model addresses one irreducible challenge in physical AI. This page covers how each works, what it's designed to achieve, and the internal benchmarks we're targeting.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0026 | paragraph | The six models inside PIC 2.0]
Designed to be the sensory foundation beneath everything else. AMDC maintains calibration across up to 14 sensor modalities at 100Hz — compensating for thermal drift, optical degradation, mechanical vibration, and EMI. Fleet-level sharing means calibration improvements propagate to every robot instantly.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0027 | paragraph | The six models inside PIC 2.0]
Gives robots calibrated awareness of what they don't know. Separates uncertainty into spatial (current sensor reliability) and temporal (world change since last update) components. Uses conformal prediction — a mathematically grounded technique — to produce confidence estimates that hold regardless of the underlying model architecture.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0028 | paragraph | The six models inside PIC 2.0]
The planning layer — designed to break complex goals into manageable sub-tasks across three hierarchical levels: Mission (hours), Strategy (minutes), Tactic (seconds). Rather than requiring explicit programming, HTD-IRL learns effective decomposition strategies from expert human demonstrations via inverse RL.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0029 | paragraph | The six models inside PIC 2.0]
The decision-making engine. Rather than judging actions against fixed thresholds, GRPO evaluates each action relative to N=16–32 sampled alternatives. This group-relative approach produces richer training signals. Safety constraints from SEOM are integrated directly into the training objective — so the policy has safety baked into what it can generate.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0030 | paragraph | The six models inside PIC 2.0]
The most architecturally novel component of PIC 2.0. Rather than applying safety as a post-hoc filter, SEOM encodes domain-specific safety rules as differentiable penalty gradients active during model training. The result: a policy that structurally cannot generate unsafe actions — they're not filtered, they were never learned. SHA-256 audit chain for full traceability.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0031 | paragraph | The six models inside PIC 2.0]
Designed to transform groups of individual robots into coordinated teams. Uses Centralised Training with Decentralised Execution (CTDE): robots train together for cooperative strategies, then each executes independently at runtime — no central coordination bottleneck, no single point of failure. Fleet calibration sharing via AMDC means the whole fleet improves from any robot's learning.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0073 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture]

See all five platforms in action

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0075 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
Fari, Senpai, Sentinel Prime AI, Aido Rover, and Aido Humanoid — all demonstrated in real environments. Watch the showcase for a hands-on view of the platforms described below.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0076 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
Designed to support older adults with health monitoring, companionship, and safety-aware autonomy in home environments — without requiring clinical infrastructure.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0077 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
Fari carries the highest SEOM penalty weight (λ=10.0) in the InGen product line — reflecting the severity of potential harms in a healthcare-adjacent context where even a single safety failure is categorically unacceptable.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0078 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
The rPPG monitoring capability detects heart rate from subtle facial skin colour changes via camera. AMDC's real-time optical calibration is essential — target accuracy degrades from ±3.1 BPM to ±8.5 BPM without it, rendering readings clinically unusable.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0079 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
EHR integration via HL7 FHIR R4 allows Fari to read medication schedules, log vital signs, and flag deviations directly within existing care record systems — no separate data silo.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0080 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
An adaptive educational robot designed to personalise learning for every student — with six specialised SEND modes and constitutional child safety constraints embedded at training time.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0081 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
Senpai's 6 SEND modes are designed as first-class features, not accessibility afterthoughts. Each mode reconfigures typography, pacing, interaction design, and content delivery to match the learner's specific profile — without requiring the student to self-identify.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0082 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
HTD-IRL enables Senpai to adapt lesson structure dynamically from expert teacher demonstrations — learning effective pedagogical sequences rather than following rigid scripts.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0083 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
A multi-sensor AI security platform designed around one key insight: reducing false alerts matters as much as improving detection. STUM's three-tier confidence gate targets 84% false alert reduction.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0084 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
Industry benchmarks commonly cited in security AI literature suggest false alert rates of ~18% for many systems. Our internal modelling targets approximately 2.8% through STUM's confidence gating — a research target, not a commercial deployment result.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0085 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
The 5-model ensemble (ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B4, MobileNetV3, ViT-Small, YOLO) runs at 6Hz on 275 TOPS, with each model contributing a confidence vote that STUM combines into a calibrated aggregate uncertainty value before alerting.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0086 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
A rugged outdoor autonomous patrol robot designed for diverse terrain and all-weather environments. IP66/67 rated, 870 lbs, designed for −40°C to +70°C operation with 25 AI detection classes.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0087 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
Rover uses GRPO N=24 — larger than indoor platforms — because outdoor patrol tasks have longer decision horizons where richer gradient signals during training are needed for robust outdoor policies.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0088 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
AMDC's outdoor calibration handles the highest drift challenge in the fleet: extreme temperature swings, vibration from rough terrain, and GPS multipath interference all require continuous correction at 100Hz to maintain reliable navigation and detection accuracy.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0089 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
Our most ambitious platform — a commercially-focused humanoid robot designed for general-purpose tasks in environments built for human form. 54 DoF, 30 manipulation skills, 14 grasp types.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0090 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
At N=32, the Humanoid uses the largest GRPO group size in the InGen lineup. Whole-body 54-DoF control is an exceptionally high-dimensional problem — requiring the richest gradient signals to develop coordinated, natural movement policies.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ORIGAMI-20260812::block-0091 | paragraph | Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action]
The Humanoid is at an earlier stage of development than our other platforms. We expect this to be a multi-year development process. All specifications here are highly preliminary design targets subject to significant revision.

source_blocks.text: Five platforms, one architecture

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture
source_blocks.text: Every InGen robot platform is being built on PIC 2.0 — the same foundation models, the same safety framework, configured for each domain. All five platforms are in active development.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: See all five platforms in action

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: Fari, Senpai, Sentinel Prime AI, Aido Rover, and Aido Humanoid — all demonstrated in real environments. Watch the showcase for a hands-on view of the platforms described below.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: Designed to support older adults with health monitoring, companionship, and safety-aware autonomy in home environments — without requiring clinical infrastructure.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: Fari carries the highest SEOM penalty weight (λ=10.0) in the InGen product line — reflecting the severity of potential harms in a healthcare-adjacent context where even a single safety failure is categorically unacceptable.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: The rPPG monitoring capability detects heart rate from subtle facial skin colour changes via camera. AMDC's real-time optical calibration is essential — target accuracy degrades from ±3.1 BPM to ±8.5 BPM without it, rendering readings clinically unusable.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: EHR integration via HL7 FHIR R4 allows Fari to read medication schedules, log vital signs, and flag deviations directly within existing care record systems — no separate data silo.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: An adaptive educational robot designed to personalise learning for every student — with six specialised SEND modes and constitutional child safety constraints embedded at training time.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: Senpai's 6 SEND modes are designed as first-class features, not accessibility afterthoughts. Each mode reconfigures typography, pacing, interaction design, and content delivery to match the learner's specific profile — without requiring the student to self-identify.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: HTD-IRL enables Senpai to adapt lesson structure dynamically from expert teacher demonstrations — learning effective pedagogical sequences rather than following rigid scripts.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: A multi-sensor AI security platform designed around one key insight: reducing false alerts matters as much as improving detection. STUM's three-tier confidence gate targets 84% false alert reduction.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: Industry benchmarks commonly cited in security AI literature suggest false alert rates of ~18% for many systems. Our internal modelling targets approximately 2.8% through STUM's confidence gating — a research target, not a commercial deployment result.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: The 5-model ensemble (ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B4, MobileNetV3, ViT-Small, YOLO) runs at 6Hz on 275 TOPS, with each model contributing a confidence vote that STUM combines into a calibrated aggregate uncertainty value before alerting.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: A rugged outdoor autonomous patrol robot designed for diverse terrain and all-weather environments. IP66/67 rated, 870 lbs, designed for −40°C to +70°C operation with 25 AI detection classes.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: Rover uses GRPO N=24 — larger than indoor platforms — because outdoor patrol tasks have longer decision horizons where richer gradient signals during training are needed for robust outdoor policies.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: AMDC's outdoor calibration handles the highest drift challenge in the fleet: extreme temperature swings, vibration from rough terrain, and GPS multipath interference all require continuous correction at 100Hz to maintain reliable navigation and detection accuracy.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: Our most ambitious platform — a commercially-focused humanoid robot designed for general-purpose tasks in environments built for human form. 54 DoF, 30 manipulation skills, 14 grasp types.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: At N=32, the Humanoid uses the largest GRPO group size in the InGen lineup. Whole-body 54-DoF control is an exceptionally high-dimensional problem — requiring the richest gradient signals to develop coordinated, natural movement policies.

source_blocks.path: Five platforms, one architecture > See all five platforms in action
source_blocks.text: The Humanoid is at an earlier stage of development than our other platforms. We expect this to be a multi-year development process. All specifications here are highly preliminary design targets subject to significant revision.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0001 | heading | Sentinel Prime AI]
Sentinel Prime AI

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0002 | paragraph | Sentinel Prime AI]
A 27-detection AI security platform combining a 5-model deep ensemble, probabilistic uncertainty quantification (STUM), and hardware-enforced ethical governance (SEOM) — designed to reduce false alert rates to sub-3% while running entirely at the edge on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0003 | heading | Sentinel Prime AI > See Sentinel In Action]
See Sentinel In Action

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0004 | heading | Sentinel Prime AI > Alert Fatigue Is Breaking Security]
Alert Fatigue Is Breaking Security

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0005 | paragraph | Sentinel Prime AI > Alert Fatigue Is Breaking Security]
Traditional AI security cameras generate false alert rates of 15–25%. At enterprise scale, that means hundreds of false alarms per day — training operators to ignore alerts entirely. Sentinel Prime AI is designed to solve this with probabilistic uncertainty quantification: if the AI is uncertain, it stays silent.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0006 | heading | Sentinel Prime AI > How Sentinel Works]
How Sentinel Works

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0007 | paragraph | Sentinel Prime AI > How Sentinel Works]
Four-tier inference pipeline: Sense → Classify → Gate → Act. Every detection passes through 14 sensors, 5 AI models, the STUM uncertainty gate, and SEOM governance rules before becoming an operator alert.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0008 | heading | Sentinel Prime AI > Four Hardware Configurations]
Four Hardware Configurations

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0009 | heading | Sentinel Prime AI > 27 Simultaneous AI Detections]
27 Simultaneous AI Detections

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0010 | paragraph | Sentinel Prime AI > 27 Simultaneous AI Detections]
All 27 detection functions designed to run simultaneously at 6Hz on a single Jetson AGX Orin. Grouped into five operational categories.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0011 | heading | The Origami AI Architecture]
The Origami AI Architecture

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0012 | paragraph | The Origami AI Architecture]
A proprietary multi-layer architecture combining a 5-model deep ensemble, probabilistic uncertainty quantification, hardware-enforced safety governance, and 14-sensor multimodal fusion — all designed to run at the edge with zero cloud dependency for inference.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0013 | heading | The Origami AI Architecture > Five AI Models, One Ensemble]
Five AI Models, One Ensemble

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0014 | paragraph | The Origami AI Architecture > Five AI Models, One Ensemble]
Five specialist TensorRT-optimised models run in parallel on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Each model addresses a specific detection modality; outputs are fused before the STUM uncertainty gate.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0015 | heading | The Origami AI Architecture > STUM Uncertainty Quantification]
STUM Uncertainty Quantification

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0016 | paragraph | The Origami AI Architecture > STUM Uncertainty Quantification]
The most commercially significant architectural innovation. By applying probabilistic uncertainty quantification to every detection, STUM directly solves the alert fatigue problem that makes traditional AI security platforms unusable at enterprise scale.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0017 | heading | The Origami AI Architecture > SEOM Safety & Ethics Framework]
SEOM Safety & Ethics Framework

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-SENTINEL-20260812::block-0018 | paragraph | The Origami AI Architecture > SEOM Safety & Ethics Framework]
10 irrevocable safety rules enforced at the FPGA hardware level. Once deployed, these rules cannot be overridden by software, configuration, or operator action. Designed for EU AI Act Article 9 compliance.

V-Model systems engineering lifecycle. 8 subsystems decomposed into 7 parallel development tracks. 34 work packages. 5 quality gates. 18-month target build timeline. All safety-critical functions designed to run on-device at 6Hz with <200ms end-to-end latency.

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI
source_blocks.text: Sentinel Prime AI

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI
source_blocks.text: A 27-detection AI security platform combining a 5-model deep ensemble, probabilistic uncertainty quantification (STUM), and hardware-enforced ethical governance (SEOM) — designed to reduce false alert rates to sub-3% while running entirely at the edge on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin.

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI > See Sentinel In Action
source_blocks.text: See Sentinel In Action

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI > Alert Fatigue Is Breaking Security
source_blocks.text: Alert Fatigue Is Breaking Security

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI > Alert Fatigue Is Breaking Security
source_blocks.text: Traditional AI security cameras generate false alert rates of 15–25%. At enterprise scale, that means hundreds of false alarms per day — training operators to ignore alerts entirely. Sentinel Prime AI is designed to solve this with probabilistic uncertainty quantification: if the AI is uncertain, it stays silent.

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI > How Sentinel Works
source_blocks.text: How Sentinel Works

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI > How Sentinel Works
source_blocks.text: Four-tier inference pipeline: Sense → Classify → Gate → Act. Every detection passes through 14 sensors, 5 AI models, the STUM uncertainty gate, and SEOM governance rules before becoming an operator alert.

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI > Four Hardware Configurations
source_blocks.text: Four Hardware Configurations

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI > 27 Simultaneous AI Detections
source_blocks.text: 27 Simultaneous AI Detections

source_blocks.path: Sentinel Prime AI > 27 Simultaneous AI Detections
source_blocks.text: All 27 detection functions designed to run simultaneously at 6Hz on a single Jetson AGX Orin. Grouped into five operational categories.

source_blocks.path: The Origami AI Architecture
source_blocks.text: The Origami AI Architecture

source_blocks.path: The Origami AI Architecture
source_blocks.text: A proprietary multi-layer architecture combining a 5-model deep ensemble, probabilistic uncertainty quantification, hardware-enforced safety governance, and 14-sensor multimodal fusion — all designed to run at the edge with zero cloud dependency for inference.

source_blocks.path: The Origami AI Architecture > Five AI Models, One Ensemble
source_blocks.text: Five AI Models, One Ensemble

source_blocks.path: The Origami AI Architecture > Five AI Models, One Ensemble
source_blocks.text: Five specialist TensorRT-optimised models run in parallel on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Each model addresses a specific detection modality; outputs are fused before the STUM uncertainty gate.

source_blocks.path: The Origami AI Architecture > STUM Uncertainty Quantification
source_blocks.text: STUM Uncertainty Quantification

source_blocks.path: The Origami AI Architecture > STUM Uncertainty Quantification
source_blocks.text: The most commercially significant architectural innovation. By applying probabilistic uncertainty quantification to every detection, STUM directly solves the alert fatigue problem that makes traditional AI security platforms unusable at enterprise scale.

source_blocks.path: The Origami AI Architecture > SEOM Safety & Ethics Framework
source_blocks.text: SEOM Safety & Ethics Framework

source_blocks.path: The Origami AI Architecture > SEOM Safety & Ethics Framework
source_blocks.text: 10 irrevocable safety rules enforced at the FPGA hardware level. Once deployed, these rules cannot be overridden by software, configuration, or operator action. Designed for EU AI Act Article 9 compliance.

source_blocks.text: Sentinel Prime AI is architected from the ground up for regulatory compliance. EU AI Act Article 9 SEOM governance, GDPR biometric handling, ISO 27001 security management, and FIPS 140-3 hardware security are design constraints — not afterthoughts.

Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure]
InGen Dynamics is building a next-generation autonomous patrol and inspection platform — designed for all-weather, multi-terrain environments where continuous human coverage isn't practical or cost-effective.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0003 | heading | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > Why autonomous outdoor robotics, why now]
Why autonomous outdoor robotics, why now

Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > A platform designed for where humans can't]
A platform designed for where humans can't

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0005 | paragraph | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > A platform designed for where humans can't]
Aido Rover is being engineered for outdoor environments as the primary design context — not an adaptation from indoor robotics. The following represent our current engineering objectives.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0006 | heading | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > Seven industries we're designing for]
Seven industries we're designing for

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0007 | paragraph | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > Seven industries we're designing for]
These are the markets we intend to serve upon successful platform development and commercialisation.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0008 | heading | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > Why we believe we can do this differently]
Why we believe we can do this differently

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0009 | paragraph | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > Why we believe we can do this differently]
Several design choices we believe create meaningful differentiation — if we execute successfully on the development programme.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0010 | heading | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > The development journey]
The development journey

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0011 | paragraph | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > The development journey]
We're committed to transparency about where Aido Rover stands today and what remains ahead. The following reflects our current planning — subject to change as engineering progresses.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0012 | heading | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > Building the future of outdoor autonomy]
Building the future of outdoor autonomy

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0013 | paragraph | Aido 
Rover 
Autonomous outdoor intelligence for the world's critical infrastructure > Building the future of outdoor autonomy]
We're in active development and welcome conversations with enterprises in our target sectors, potential partners, and those interested in learning more about InGen Dynamics and the Aido Rover programme.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0014 | heading | Platform Technology]
Platform Technology

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0015 | paragraph | Platform Technology]
Engineering specifications and design objectives for Aido Rover. All information here represents current design targets and intended capabilities — not commercially validated performance.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0016 | heading | Platform Technology > Platform hardware design targets]
Platform hardware design targets

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0017 | heading | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design]
14-sensor design

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0018 | paragraph | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design]
Designed across 7 modalities with no single point of failure. Component choices subject to change during development.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0019 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 1]
ID | Sensor | Intended Role | Target Rate | Status

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0020 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 2]
S01 | LiDAR 360° Primary VLP-32C class · 32-beam · 200m target | Primary navigation, 3D mapping, obstacle detection, perimeter monitoring, digital twin data generation. | 10 Hz target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0021 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 3]
S02 | LiDAR Forward Livox class · 25Hz target | High-frequency forward obstacle detection between primary scans. Safety proximity gate support. | 25 Hz target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0022 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 4]
S03 | 4K PTZ Camera Sony IMX class · 4K@30fps · 30× optical | Visual detection R01–R15, evidence recording, automated subject tracking on confirmed events. | 30 fps target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0023 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 5]
S04 | Stereo RGB-D ZED 2i class · 1080p stereo · 20m depth | Secondary SLAM layer visual odometry. Person and face detection at designed close ranges. | 20 fps target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0024 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 6]
S05 | Night Vision NIR 0.001 lux target · 4K · 940nm IR invisible | Night patrol capability without visible light emission — no position reveal to subjects. | 30 fps target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0025 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 7]
S06 | FLIR Thermal LWIR FLIR Lepton class · 640×480@30fps | Person through fog/smoke, solar panel thermal inspection, equipment overheating, fire pre-ignition. | 30 fps target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0026 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 8]
S07 | Multispectral 5-Band MicaSense class · 475/560/668/840/717nm | Solar anomaly detection, NDVI/NDRE/NDWI crop mapping, vegetation fire risk assessment. | On-demand | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0027 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 9]
S08 | Acoustic Array 8-Mic 8× MEMS · 360° · ±5° bearing target | Acoustic event classification — gunshot and drone rotor signatures. Bearing accuracy subject to validation. | Continuous | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0028 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 10]
S09 | 24GHz FMCW Radar TI IWR1843 class · 150m target | All-weather complement to optical — designed to maintain capability through rain and dense fog. | 50 Hz target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0029 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 11]
S10 | Gas Sensor Array Electrochemical · CH₄/H₂S/CO/O₂/VOC | Gas leak detection in industrial environments. Hardware safety relay cuts motors on LEL detection. | 1 Hz target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0030 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 12]
S11 | Environmental Station Wind · Temp · Humidity · Pressure | Real-time environmental data feeding the uncertainty scoring system for dynamic sensor weighting. | 1 Hz target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0031 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 13]
S12 | IMU 9-DOF TDK ICM-42688-P class · 1kHz target | Master timing reference, wheel slip detection, GPS dead-reckoning fallback during signal gaps. | 1 kHz target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0032 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 14]
S13 | GPS / RTK Dual-band GPS/RTK · 10Hz target | Primary positioning layer. Designed to fall back to LiDAR place recognition when GPS quality degrades. | 10 Hz target | In development

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0033 | table_row | Platform Technology > 14-sensor design > row 15]
S14 | Deterrent System LED searchlights · Siren · Speaker | Safety-gated deterrent — activation requires high-confidence human detection before any engagement. | On-command | In development

25 planned detection functions

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0035 | paragraph | Platform Technology > 25 planned detection functions]
Design objectives for AI detection capabilities. All models are in development — performance figures are targets requiring independent validation before commercial claims can be made.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0036 | heading | Our company]
Our company

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0037 | paragraph | Our company]
InGen Dynamics has been building AI and robotics since 2015. Aido Rover is our most ambitious programme — taking a decade of platform experience into outdoor autonomous intelligence.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0038 | paragraph | Our company]
Founded in 2015 by Arshad Hisham, InGen Dynamics has developed and distributed indoor service robots globally, built the Origami AI Platform, and delivered the Sentinel enterprise security platform. Aido Rover represents our next chapter.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0039 | heading | Our company > Products we've shipped]
Products we've shipped

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0040 | paragraph | Our company > Products we've shipped]
Aido Rover is being built on the proven foundations of these established InGen Dynamics platforms.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0041 | heading | Our company > We believe robotics and AI have the potential to genuinely improve lives]
We believe robotics and AI have the potential to genuinely improve lives

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0042 | paragraph | Our company > We believe robotics and AI have the potential to genuinely improve lives]
Not theoretically — practically. Reducing the number of people working dangerous outdoor security shifts in all-weather conditions. Making solar infrastructure perform as designed. Detecting gas leaks before they become incidents. That's what Aido Rover is being built to do.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0043 | heading | Let's connect]
Let's connect

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-ROVER-20260812::block-0044 | paragraph | Let's connect]
Aido Rover is in development and we're building relationships with enterprises in our target sectors. If you represent an organisation in our target markets, or have a general enquiry, we'd welcome the conversation.

The Aido Humanoid is designed to operate in standard human environments without structural modification — doorways, corridors, stairs, lifts, and shared workspaces.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0010 | paragraph | Human‑scale. 
Human‑safe.

6-DOF ankle, 3-DOF knee, 6-DOF hip per side. Harmonic drive actuators with integrated torque sensors. Designed for flat terrain, slopes ≤15°, and standard stairs.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0011 | paragraph | Human‑scale.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0068 | paragraph | Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > GR00T N1.6]
NVIDIA's humanoid foundation model providing whole-body motor control, cross-embodiment transfer learning, and sim-to-real capability. Trained on Isaac Lab simulation with 98% successful transfer rate (design target). Accepts multimodal input: joint state, RGB-D, force/torque, and language tokens.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0069 | heading | Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > GRPO Policy Optimisation]
GRPO Policy Optimisation

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0070 | paragraph | Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > GRPO Policy Optimisation]
Group Relative Policy Optimisation fine-tunes GR00T for vertical-specific behaviour. N=16 candidate rollouts, γ=0.985 discount, advantage computed against group mean. Healthcare and eldercare policies receive the highest SEOM λ weighting (10.0).

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0071 | heading | Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > Origami AI Platform]

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0072 | paragraph | Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > Origami AI Platform]
Enterprise customers can build vertical-specific skill libraries and deploy over-the-air. Origami NLP handles multi-language voice command processing across 40+ languages in the designed interaction layer. Modular skill architecture avoids full model retraining.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0073 | heading | Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > STUM — designed to know its own limits.]
STUM — designed to know its own limits.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0074 | paragraph | Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > STUM — designed to know its own limits.]
A core design principle: the Humanoid should recognise and communicate uncertainty rather than attempt tasks when confidence falls below a safe threshold.

SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level.

[SOURCE_BLOCK PUB-HUMANOID-20260812::block-0076 | paragraph | Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level.]

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > GR00T N1.6
source_blocks.text: NVIDIA's humanoid foundation model providing whole-body motor control, cross-embodiment transfer learning, and sim-to-real capability. Trained on Isaac Lab simulation with 98% successful transfer rate (design target). Accepts multimodal input: joint state, RGB-D, force/torque, and language tokens.

source_blocks.text: GRPO Policy Optimisation

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > Three layers of intelligence. > GRPO Policy Optimisation
source_blocks.text: Group Relative Policy Optimisation fine-tunes GR00T for vertical-specific behaviour. N=16 candidate rollouts, γ=0.985 discount, advantage computed against group mean. Healthcare and eldercare policies receive the highest SEOM λ weighting (10.0).

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level.
source_blocks.text: These 12 rules form the designed safety envelope. They are engineering design requirements, not demonstrated performance benchmarks.

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 1
source_blocks.text: ID | Rule | Design Intent | Priority

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 2
source_blocks.text: H01 | Force Limit 5N max contact force design target | Monitored via wrist F/T sensors and joint torque feedback. Designed for 1kHz enforcement. | Highest

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 3
source_blocks.text: H02 | Speed Near Humans 0.1 m/s max within 0.5m | Real-time MPC velocity envelope enforcement. All sensor modalities for proximity detection. | All verticals

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 4
source_blocks.text: H03 | Personal Space 4-zone proxemic model | Public (3.6m) / Social (1.2m) / Personal (0.45m) / Intimate (0.15m). Context-appropriate. | Context-sensitive

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 5
source_blocks.text: H04 | Gaze Signalling Pre-action intent communication | Head orient + LED + verbal narration before near-human manipulation. 0.8s minimum dwell. | Social compliance

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 6
source_blocks.text: H05 | Medication Safety Triple-check protocol | Patient ID → medication verify → verbal confirm → consent — each step required. | Healthcare only

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 7
source_blocks.text: H06 | Graceful Degradation Fail-safe posture on any critical failure | Controlled kneel → sit → inform caregiver. Never free-fall. Battery reserve for safe shutdown. | All verticals

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 8
source_blocks.text: H07 | Night Mode Reduced sensory output 22:00–06:00 | Whisper volume, dimmed LEDs, projected-only output, no projector flash. | Eldercare

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 9
source_blocks.text: H08 | Fall Prevention Predictive intervention if gait anomaly detected | Pre-positioned support within 1.2m before fall occurs. 3.2s target response time. | Healthcare + Eldercare

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 10
source_blocks.text: H09 | Privacy Zones No recording in bathrooms/changing areas | Geofenced privacy areas with vision disabled. Audio-only for emergency detection. | All verticals

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 11
source_blocks.text: H10 | Consent Gate Affirmative consent before physical contact | Multimodal consent: verbal + gesture + face. No assumption from previous sessions. | All verticals

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 12
source_blocks.text: H11 | Uncertainty Halt Autonomous escalation when σ exceeds k | STUM σ threshold triggers pause → explain → escalate sequence. | STUM σ ≥ threshold

source_blocks.path: Inside the Aido Humanoid. > SEOM — 12 safety rules embedded at training level. > row 13
source_blocks.text: H12 | Audit Completeness 100% action logging with tamper-evident chain | Timestamps, sensor readings, SEOM states, decision rationale. EU AI Act Art.9 export. | EU AI Act mandatory
